question.text: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. At the mean position, velocity of the particle is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The distance of the particle from the mean position when its speed becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>α</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo></math>______.

solution.text:
The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle at the mean position is given by

V=Aω   ...1

From equation (1), it follows that

10=4×ω⇒ω=52 rad s-1

The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle at any instantaneous position x can be expressed as

v=ωA2-x2   ...2

From equation (2), it follows that

5=5242-x2⇒x2=16-4=12⇒x=12 cm

Hence, α=12.
